subject: religious-studies
title: Religion: Conflict, Cohesion and Freedom
welcome_lead: Religion has bound communities and torn them apart. Examine both sides — and the freedom of belief.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: religion's role in conflict, cohesion and freedom of belief.
final_note: You have studied religion as glue and as fire. Freedom of belief remains a fragile human right.

concepts.def: Bonds and trust that hold a community together; religions can foster both bonding and bridging capital.
Conflict in which religious identity, doctrine or institutions play a significant role.
Universal Declaration of Human Rights protecting freedom of thought, conscience and religion.
Laws criminalising speech offensive to religion; debated for freedom of expression implications.
Divisions and conflict between branches of the same religion, e.g. Sunni-Shia.
Restoration of relationships after conflict, often involving religious actors and rituals.

walkthroughs.body_html: Religious communities provide identity, mutual aid, education and meaning. Robert Putnam's research distinguishes bonding (within-group) and bridging (across-group) capital, both nurtured by congregational life and interfaith initiatives.

Conflicts in Northern Ireland, the Balkans, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Iraq and Myanmar involve religion intertwined with politics and ethnicity. Mark Juergensmeyer's research highlights how religious imagery can sanctify violence; political and economic grievances usually underlie conflict.

UDHR Article 18 and ICCPR Article 18 protect freedom of religion or belief. Blasphemy laws (Pakistan, some Gulf states), restrictions on minorities (Bahá'í in Iran, Uyghur Muslims in Xinjiang) and rising hate crimes pose challenges. Religious actors also serve in reconciliation (South Africa TRC, Mozambique).

mcqs.q: What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.
Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.

options: The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.

You should do whatever feels right in the moment.
